etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin praemātūrus, equivalent to pre- +‎ mature. Attested circa 1520.

definitions.definition: Occurring before a state of readiness or maturity has arrived.
Taking place earlier than anticipated, prepared for, or desired.

quote.citation: 1844, Edgar Allan Poe, The Premature Burial:
quote.text: I was lost in reveries of death, and the idea of premature burial held continual possession of my brain.
